$comment: AUTHORITY for why a client that read a launcher's discovery document (specs/src/discovery/DiscoveryDocument.json) found no launcher: each reason as every SDK spells it, and what it means. A reader shows an absent launcher by its reason, and an absent launcher is not one that manages nothing, so a reason means one thing in every language. Kotlin (packages/kotlin/sdk/src/main/kotlin/semiont/discovery/Discovery.kt) is held to this table by packages/kotlin/sdk/src/test/kotlin/semiont/discovery/DiscoveryTest.kt. TypeScript (packages/typescript/sdk/src/discovery.ts), Rust (packages/rust/sdk/src/discovery.rs), Python (packages/python/sdk/src/semiont/discovery.py) and Go (packages/go/sdk/discovery/discovery.go) state the reasons by hand.

reasons.docs: There is no document where it was looked for: no file, an HTTP status that is not success, or a page that is not JSON.
There is a document, and it is not JSON.
It is JSON, and not a discovery document: one entry that is not what the schema says makes the whole document invalid, since a partial reading would hide a running knowledge base without a trace.
It is a discovery document of a version this client does not speak, and is not read in part.
It could not be read at all: the file could not be opened or decoded, or the request got no answer by its deadline.
